page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 7 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. A notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory subsystem performance; while cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, ranking in the bottom 25%. Write bandwidth for large blocks remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core execution speed offer predictable compute performance for workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The instance is suited for compute-bound tasks such as text processing, web serving, and software compilation. However, applications requiring high-throughput, large-scale memory access may be constrained by the lower uncached memory read bandwidth.
